properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-10-24, choosing the recommendation: "Yes, one 'open breach'": every recorded breach still standing (an open defect finding, an exceeded budget on a non-KPP limit, a VIOLATES edge into a Constraint, an environment-rule violation ruled must-fix) is one reading: a gap and a line of the open-work report until something closes it.

THE QUESTION. Measured on main 61c05ad74, a recorded breach reached the loop only in two narrow forms: a KPP's exceeded budget (kpp_breached) and an untriaged environment-rule violation (open_violation). An open defect finding, an exceeded budget on an ordinary limit, a VIOLATES edge into a Constraint and a violation ruled `rejected` (must fix) reached no gap and no line of `next`, so the Shop sample's barn 12 ft from the well (100 ft limit) and SeattleArch's roof 3 7/16" over its height maximum both read "nothing open".

WHAT IT MEANS. One `open_breach` gap per breach, and loop_status counts the unruled ones in a `next` line of their own (`breaches_open`, the newest 20 listed in `breaches` with their kind). Each closes its own way: a defect finding by INVALIDATES from the change or decision that fixed it, or valid_to (a decision that only rests on it does not close it); an exceeded limit when its readings fit; a VIOLATES edge when removed; a must-fix violation by `resolved_at` on its edge, or a waiver. Any of them stands on purpose by a ruling: acknowledging its gap with the reason. A KPP keeps kpp_breached and an untriaged violation keeps open_violation, so nothing is asked twice.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-24: every recorded breach still standing is one reading, an open breach: a gap and a line of the open-work report until something closes it
